hero.subtitle: A fall at a Stanton shopping center or apartment complex can leave you with medical bills and unanswered questions about who's responsible. LawProactive connects you, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles premises liability claims in Orange County.

about.title: Stanton Premises Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Stanton is a compact, busy city packed into a few square miles of Orange County, with retail plazas and residential complexes clustered along Beach Boulevard and Katella Avenue. When a property owner lets a spill, broken step, or poor lighting go unaddressed, the people who shop, work, or live there can pay the price. California law requires an injured person to show the property owner knew, or reasonably should have known, about the hazard and failed to act. That's why what happens right after a fall matters — photos of the hazard, witness names, and store surveillance footage can all fade or disappear quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves; we connect Stanton residents hurt on someone else's property with an independent attorney who can evaluate the claim, gather evidence, and explain your options. There's no cost to find out where you stand, and no fee unless the attorney recovers money for you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to an Insurer

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or should have known about the hazard. An attorney knows what evidence — inspection logs, prior complaints, maintenance records — can establish that.

items.title: Video and Physical Evidence Disappear Fast
items.desc: Many Stanton retailers and complexes overwrite surveillance footage within days. Acting quickly to send a preservation request can be the difference between having proof and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Reduce, Not Erase, Your Claim
items.desc: Even if a property owner argues you weren't watching where you stepped, California's pure comparative fault rule still allows you to recover a reduced amount based on the degree of fault assigned to each side.

items.question: I slipped at a store on Beach Boulevard — what should I do first?
items.answer: Report the fall to store management and ask that an incident report be made, then photograph the hazard before it's cleaned up or fixed. If there are security cameras nearby, note their location, since footage may only be kept for a short time. Getting medical care and connecting with an attorney early helps preserve that evidence.

items.question: How long do I have to file a premises liability claim in California?
items.answer: Generally you have two years from the date of the fall to file a lawsuit, but that window shrinks significantly if a government entity owns or maintains the property. Because Stanton has a mix of private plazas and public sidewalks and facilities, it's worth confirming ownership early so no deadline is missed.

items.question: Will it hurt my case if I wasn't paying attention when I fell?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California uses a pure comparative fault system, meaning your compensation can be reduced by your percentage of fault rather than eliminated entirely. An independent attorney can help assess how fault might be divided based on the specific hazard and circumstances.
